text:
Am I the only one who thinks the sulfur cube is trash?

Am I the only one who thinks the sulfur cube is trash? I feel like it's completely pointless. Yes you can do the boat thing and it's a different way of adding half slabs. But at this point with Mojang drops I feel like nothing is unique anymore. I think that they try so hard to add things that don't exist in any mod and no one has done before that they forget about the actual problems of their game.
For example, last year Mojang "solved" the problem of transporting entities and building in the air with the happy ghast. Alr, fair. Not my favorite but ig it does the trick. Or the sorting problem, they first tried with allays and since they didn't solve the problem they tried with copper golems. Hopper sorters are still the best way to sort items.
My guess is that sulfur cube tried to solve the half slab thing that the community has been asking for since forever, but in my opinion this behavior of trying to fix problems with new mobs or entities just doesn't work. If for some reason you want to decorate smth with let's say dirt slabs, sure you can use the sulfur cube but are you rlly gonna use more than, idk, 10? Bc let's remember they are entities, not actual slabs, which means if u want a lot of slabs they will cause lots of lag.
I feel like since Mojang+Microsoft has basically won capitalism they just settled on mediocrity. They don't need to make cool updates because they will keep making money either way and Minecraft will be the most sold game anyways, even if they didn't update it anymore.

In my opinion I'd prefer to have one year of no updates and have a big update on 2027 that solves the inventory problem in a clever way (without adding more entities pls) rather than frequent drops with pointless implementations.
Yes, there are 2 new blocks with all their stairs, slabs, etc. variants. But do we really need those? "But they're great for builders" someone might say... Bruh builders already have plenty of blocks to build with, and sulfur caves are just pointless. The two new blocks are pointless just like the sulfur cube.
On the other hand, I really like the fact that they've been announcing since some time ago "Hey, we're working on updating from OpenGL to Vulkan, this will take some time so don't expect it to be until (insert amount of time here lol)." Dude I love them communicating us these kind of stuff.
I'd love to see one Minecraft post saying smth like "Hey, the next drops won't have as much content because we're spending most of our time and resources towards solving the inventory problem, don't expect it to be anytime soon, but we're working on it". Bro I swear this would make me so happy. I'm talking ab the inventory problem as an example but if you replace anywhere in this post "Inventory problem" with "End update" it's literally the same. Two examples of the same neglect.
I'd rather have a drop that's only bug fixes and technical changes rather than a new mob and two more blocks. For me it's way more important to fix the game as it is now, instead of adding new stuff.

Notch I will never forgive you for selling your game to Microsoft. This is the very moment when everything started to go sideways. But that's besides the point.
All in all, I think I am never gonna play any Minecraft version that doesn't start with 1.x.x and I will never update my server version to any of these new versions and the ones that will come because not only they completely lack content and are absolutely pointless, but I'm openly protesting against the way Microsoft is managing the most sold game in history. I am fed up of waiting for smth to happen, it's been years and years in silence but I can't stand Mojang anymore.
If you think like me and you thought of some clever or genius way of protesting against the aberration they're making to their game, comment it down below. We have to do smth as a community. And if you've read this much, whoa, let me congratulate u. I wrote this post using 0 AI so I appreciate you reading it until the end. That also means your dopamine receptors are just fine so well done.

text:
The Baby Model Redesign update is a testament to how frivolous the “pixel consistency” effort is.

Big rant warning. TL;DR at bottom.

So we’ve all seen the latest baby mob models and.. they’re pretty bad. I’ve been pretty accepting of most of them up to this point but there’s only so much leeway you can Mojang with these before it becomes mental gymnastics.
So the prime culprits to the outrage are the Baby Villager and Baby Zombie. Their head-to-body ratio is completely off to what it once was as their heads are much bigger than their bodies. (and Baby Zombies don’t fit in one-block gaps anymore but that’s a bug that will be patched later so I’m not worried about it) The Villager in particular also looks identical to the adult model just cut off at the bottom.
People have been asking for Mojang to shrink the heads, but there’s a glaring problem that I don’t think enough people are talking about that makes this more complicated than it appears on the surface.
For the past year or so, Mojang has been trying to fix the problem of “pixel consistency”. What is that you ask? It’s the problem of various mob textures having different sized pixels that make them either smaller or bigger than the pixels in block textures. Obviously having different sized pixels is a cardinal sin so Mojang has been tirelessly at work to purge this evil out of the game. (prime example being the retexturing of the Ghast whenever they added the Happy Ghast)
The reason the heads of the Baby Zombie and Villager are so big is not what most people think. A lot of people think Mojang thinks “big head = cute,” but there’s more to it than that. The reason the heads are big compared to the body is because they use an 8x8 texture. The issue of pixel consistency is in full force here because that’s how big the heads have to be to use an 8x8 texture.
If you were to shrink the heads it would force them to use 6x6 textures instead, which would reduce the amount of detail you can do for the face and force them to have 1-pixel eyes. Notice how many baby mobs up to this point have 1-pixel eyes. The Baby Zombie and Villager are the first mobs in the bunch to use 2-pixel eyes. (also look at the Baby Piglin texture. 1-pixel eyes are used there too)
1-pixel eyes work well for the baby animals because you can get away with them looking “cute” if you design your textures right. But this does not work for the Villager. You might could get away with the Baby Zombie having 1-pixel eyes, but I doubt it would happen. For the Baby Villager however there’s absolutely no way to make it not look like a demon spawn because it’s a humanoid mob.
And like I said, the issue is not Mojang’s design specifically, but rather because of their insistence on the problem of pixel consistency. And there’s not that many solutions here.
To shrink the head you’d either need to make the body bigger, (which would increase the size of the mob itself which comes with its own set of problems) make the head a 6x6 texture, or change every single block in the game to support 24x24 or 32x32 textures so you can shrink your base pixel size so you can shrink the head that way. Or you leave the head like it is and make it look terrible.
By latching onto the idea of pixel consistency being a problem, they’ve created a perfect storm where they’ve painted themselves into a corner. There’s no perfect solution. The pixel-count smaller mobs severely limits their design capabilities because as everyone who’s worked with pixel art knows; smaller things lead to less pixels which lead to less detail. Their only solution at this point that I feel is in their best interest is to abandon the idea of pixel consistency altogether.
TL;DR: Mojang’s design of Baby Zombies and Baby Villagers and them having bigger heads highlights the issues of their fight for “pixel consistency” as it severely limits their design ability to make smaller mobs look good. They would probably be better off abandoning the idea of pixel consistency.

text:
A bundle suggestion

I suggest that bundles should be able to hold four stackable items, 32 items that are normally stackable to 16 (ex eggs and ender pearls).
These can also be combined with normal stackable items in that a non-stackable item takes up 16 of the 64 limit, while a 16-stackable item takes up 2. You can see a potential combination in the photo. (1 unstackable x 16) + (8 16-stackable items x 2) + 32 normal items = 64.

Edit:

I am aware of what bundles are for, and I enjoy and use them. That’s why I specifically did not suggest holding more than 64 of normal items.
This suggestion is specifically to address a separate issue that a builder using as many blocks available needs 11 slots for their tools in their regular gameplay.

That’s why this suggestion is biased toward unstackable items.

text:
Bundles need more appreciation.

So many people make the mistake of just looking at a bundle as a shulker box with 1 slot, when they could not be more wrong... And what's worse is a lot of them then go on to complain about the game not having enough inventory space.
People, you're supposed to mix and match items in your bundles! The smaller the stacks of items you put in the better and you'd be surprised how much space it saves if you do it right, especially if you have more than 1! It's a balanced and cheap solution that allows you to save tons of inventory space while not giving you the OP ability that shulkers do.
It feels obvious but many people clearly don't know about it, as Grian was complaining about it a lot on stream a few days ago, and in his Hytale stream. Lots of people were agreeing as well and were confused about how bundles work so I just had to spread the good word of bundles!
